slot.brief: For a combustion reaction with given ΔU, compute ΔH using Δng of gases; direct substitution with R in appropriate units.

stem: For the combustion reaction $2\text{CO}(g)+\text{O}_2(g)\rightarrow2\text{CO}_2(g)$ at $250$ K, $\Delta U=-560$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ for the reaction as written. Take $R=8.0$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$. Find $\Delta H$.

verdicts.working: For the reaction as written, Δn_g = 2 − 3 = −1. Thus ΔH = ΔU + Δn_gRT = −560 kJ mol⁻¹ − (8.0 × 250 / 1000) kJ mol⁻¹ = −562 kJ mol⁻¹.

working:
$\Delta n_g=2-(2+1)=-1$\n$\Delta H=\Delta U+\Delta n_gRT$\n$=-560+\dfrac{(-1)(8.0)(250)}{1000}=-562$ kJ mol$^{-1}$

Independent check: For the reaction as written, Δn_g = 2 − 3 = −1. Thus ΔH = ΔU + Δn_gRT = −560 kJ mol⁻¹ − (8.0 × 250 / 1000) kJ mol⁻¹ = −562 kJ mol⁻¹.
